correctness.rationale: Proof is reconstructed: increasing injectivity forces idempotent targets to be partial identities; square roots fix exactly their target points; moving domain and image disjoint and split at fixed points; each gap contributes the central trinomial count by disjoint-domain-and-image choices. Uniform-target log-fiber mgf has analytic generating series B_t(z)/(1-zB_t(z)), a unique simple pole near z=1/2, giving explicit positive renewal-reward cumulants and a Gaussian CLT by mgf convergence. Independent brute-force enumeration covers all increasing partial maps n<=9, all individual target fibers and coefficient counts; a separately differentiated recurrence tests large-n cumulants. Finite checks are supporting, not universal proof.

value.rationale: Square-root fibers are a natural semigroup-theoretic statistic attached to individual idempotents; rank totals do not distinguish their position-dependent multiplicities (already 19 versus 9 for equal-rank targets in P_5). The log-root Gaussian law and exponential arithmetic-versus-typical discrepancy characterize the entire natural random-target model in arbitrary degree, revealing structurally different behavior from extensive-only Motzkin fibers. This is more than a known-table recomputation, and the familiar generating-function and renewal steps are credited as techniques rather than claimed discoveries.
